title: checkwash findings JSON, checkwash_findings_version 2
description: The document that `checkwash check --format json` writes to standard output, as UTF-8 bytes, when it exits 0 (pass) or 1 (block); with `--emit-ir` it writes the IR instead. On exit 2, a usage, input or engine error, do not read standard output as this document; the reason is on standard error. A release can add optional keys without changing checkwash_findings_version, so a consumer must ignore keys it does not know; checkwash's own tests reject any key it emits that this schema does not declare. The contract and its change rules are in docs/stability.md; embedding guidance is in docs/embedding.md.

checkwash_findings_version.description: The version of this document's shape, 2 since v0.3.0. It changes when a key is removed, renamed or changes meaning, or a required key is added, and such a change comes with a minor release. It does not change for an optional key, a new rule id or label, or a fingerprint change.

findings.description: Every finding, including those an exemption covers (`allowlisted` true) and those below the blocking threshold. The order is deterministic for one version, but it is not a contract across versions.

skipped_files.description: Repository-relative paths of files checkwash could not parse on the base or the head side (currently Python files only).

config_errors.description: Problems with the base side's checkwash configuration or exemption ledger: a file that could not be parsed, in which case defaults or no exemptions are in effect, and configuration values that are not valid. Display text.

verdict.description: `block` when a finding no exemption covers reaches the effective `fail_on` severity (`--fail-on`, else the base side's `gate.fail_on`, else `high`), otherwise `pass`. The threshold is not recorded in this document. Exit status 1 goes with `block` and 0 with `pass`.

unread.description: From the next minor (unreleased, #454): changed sides over the source size limit that no detector had to read, the sides the standard-error notes name, one entry per side, sorted by path, then side. The change holding a listed side was set aside whole, its readable side included, so a `pass` says nothing about that change. Not every set-aside path is listed; docs/stability.md says which are not. The key is omitted when there is none, and releases before the one that adds it never write it, so its absence alone does not show that every changed file was read.

base.description: The base revision label: an abbreviated commit id, whose length follows Git's settings, or the merge base of an A...B range. Not a timestamp.

head.description: The head revision label: an abbreviated commit id, or `worktree` when no range is given and the working tree is checked.

checkwash_version.description: The checkwash version that wrote the document. A build from unreleased source can report the previous release's number.

rule.description: A rule id from SPEC.md §4, or EXEMPTION_ADDED. Ids are never renamed or reused, but new ids can appear without a version change.

severity.description: Detectors report `warn`; only checkwash's gating moves a finding to `info`, `high` or `critical`.

message.description: An explanation for people. Display it and do not parse it; its wording can change in any release.

path.description: The repository-relative path, with forward slashes. For EXEMPTION_ADDED, the path of an exemption ledger the diff added to.

unit.description: The test the finding is about: a Python qualified name, with `#N` appended when several same-named definitions remain, `<suite>` for a conftest-wide control, or a JavaScript test title, which can contain `/`, `.` and spaces. Null for a finding about a whole file.

before.description: Evidence from the base side, or null.

after.description: Evidence from the head side, a description of the change where the head side has none (a removed workflow), or null.

escalators.description: Labels gating attached when it raised the severity, most of them described in SPEC.md §5, and GUARDRAIL_CREATED, which marks a newly created guardrail file left at `warn`. New labels can appear without a version change.

deescalators.description: Labels for the evidence gating found to hold or lower the severity, most of them described in SPEC.md §5. A later ORACLE_FREEZE escalation overrides them, so a `high` finding can carry one, and an inert conftest `pytestmark` is lowered to `info` with none. `ALLOWLISTED` marks a finding an exemption covers. New labels can appear without a version change.

fingerprint.description: The finding's identity, the key an exemption records. Compare it for equality and do not parse it: the unit part can contain `/`. When fingerprints change is described in docs/stability.md and docs/embedding.md.

allowlisted.description: True when an active exemption read from the base side covers the finding. Such a finding never blocks, and it stays in `findings` and in `summary`.

strength_drop.description: ASSERT_WEAKENED only: how far the assertion's strength fell. 999 is a marker, not a distance: an inverted or contradicting assertion, a reversed bound, or a replacement checkwash cannot verify, none of which is ever a mild weakening. Null for other rules.

strength_after.description: ASSERT_WEAKENED only: the strength the assertion landed on, or null when it is unknown. Null for other rules.

subject_changed.description: ASSERT_WEAKENED only: whether the assertion's subject was rewritten as well as its check, or null when an operand is unbound. It is also false when neither side recorded a subject, as for a bare truthy assert. Null for other rules.

shape.description: TEST_DISABLED only: the kind of event, such as `unit_removed`, `marker_added`, `collection_control`, `guard_weakened`, `param_cases_removed` or `inert_mark`. Null for other rules. New kinds can appear without a version change.

text.description: The source text checkwash read, or a short description of what it read. It need not equal the text at `span`.

span.description: [start, end) offsets, in Unicode code points, into the text of the file the evidence was read from, on that side, after a UTF-8 byte order mark is removed, bytes that are not UTF-8 become U+FFFD, and CRLF and CR line endings become LF. That file is usually `path`, but an assertion inherited from a conftest fixture or an imported helper, and a skip in a conftest fixture's setup, keep their span in that other file, which this document does not name. [0, 0] means no location.

summary.description: How many entries of `findings` have each severity, allowlisted ones included. This is not the number of blocking findings.

unread_side.description: One side checkwash did not read, with exactly the four facts of its standard-error note.

path.description: The repository-relative path of that side, with forward slashes.

side.description: `base` for the base revision, `head` for the head revision of a range, or `worktree` for the working tree when no range is given.

size.description: The side's size in bytes, over `limit`. A worktree side's size is its size on disk.

limit.description: The source size limit in bytes, 1,000,000 today.
